text: Understanding databases is essential for managing information effectively. There are two main types: SQL and NoSQL. SQL databases store data in tables with rows and columns, which makes them great for organized, related data. NoSQL databases are more flexible and handle large amounts of unstructured data. To get information from a database, you use queries—special commands that ask for specific data. Data modeling helps you plan how data is structured and connected before you build anything. Finally, indexes make searching faster, like a book's index, so queries return results quickly. Choosing the right type and design depends on your needs.
